rounds.text: Mohini Health & Hygiene Ltd trades at a steep discount with a price-to-book ratio of 0.68x on a book value of ₹ 49.5 against a share price of ₹ 33.8 [E1]. This deep asset discount is further highlighted by a provider key-ratios P/B of 0.75x, which looks remarkably cheap when compared against the sector benchmark of 3.01x [E5]. At a modest market capitalization of ₹ 61.7 Cr, the current valuation sits near the bottom of its yearly spectrum at just 17% of the way up its 52-week range [E2, E4]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -14%, reflecting persistent near-term top-line contraction [E11]. Conceded: the company records a negative ROCE of -2.7% and a negative ROE of -7.3% [E6, E7]. However, the current micro-cap pricing leaves an immense margin of safety for an asset base trading well below liquidation value relative to broader sector multiples.

Mohini Health & Hygiene Ltd suffers from severe fundamental destruction, evidenced by a negative return on capital employed of -2.7% and a negative return on equity of -7.3% [E6, E7]. Top-line growth has completely collapsed over every measurable timeframe, featuring compounded sales growth of 2% over 10 years, 1% over 5 years, -9% over 3 years, and a staggering -14% over the trailing twelve months, which is starkly inferior to the sector median sales growth of 17.9% [E8, E9, E10, E11, E60]. Furthermore, the business is flagged for poor sales growth of 1.34% over the past five years and a year-over-year sales contraction of 28%, accompanied by decelerating earnings growth [E50, E54, E55]. This operational deterioration is compounded by a total absence of shareholder returns through dividends, sitting at 0.00% [E3]. Expectations are dangerously detached from underlying delivery, with price growth recently exceeding profit growth by 131% while the stock languishes at just 17% of its 52-week range [E4, E45]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio of 0.68x to 0.75x sits well below the sector benchmark of 3.01x [E1, E5].

Conceded: negative returns on capital and equity [E6, E7], declining sales growth across periods [E8, E9, E10, E11, E50, E54], decelerating earnings [E55], and zero dividends [E3]. Conceded: price growth exceeding profit growth by 131% [E45] and the stock sitting at 17% of its 52-week range [E4]. However, these well-publicized operational headwinds are already deeply discounted by the market, creating an extraordinary margin of safety. The equity trades at a steep price-to-book ratio of 0.68x on filed statements, or 0.75x against a sector benchmark of 3.01x, meaning assets are heavily discounted [E1, E5]. With a market capitalization of just ₹ 61.7 Cr [E2] operating within a sector enjoying a median sales growth of 17.9% [E60], the extreme pessimism is entirely priced in.

Conceded: the price-to-book ratio stands at 0.68x on filed statements and 0.75x against a sector benchmark of 3.01x [E1, E5], alongside a market capitalization of ₹ 61.7 Cr [E2] and a sector median sales growth of 17.9% [E60]. However, calling this a "margin of safety" misinterprets the fundamental destruction of shareholder value rather than a cheap valuation. The company generates a negative ROCE of -2.7% and a negative ROE of -7.3% [E6, E7], meaning the discounted assets are actively eroding rather than compounding. Far from a temporary discount, the declining top line—with compounded sales growth dropping to 1% over 5 years, -9% over 3 years, and -14% over the trailing twelve months [E9, E10, E11]—shows a business in terminal contraction that cannot capitalize on the broader sector's 17.9% median growth [E60]. Furthermore, price growth exceeding profit growth by 131% [E45] proves that expectations are still running ahead of delivery despite the stock sitting at just 17% of its 52-week range [E4], leaving zero room for optimism. With zero dividend yield [E3] and accelerating negative screens including a 28% YoY sales drop and decelerating earnings [E54, E55], this asset discount is fully justified by ongoing operational decay.
